newsitem.title: USA: Bill for Minn. Twins stadium to drop cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: Bill for Minn. Twins stadium to drop cigarette tax.

text.p: Legislation for financing a new stadium for the Minnesota Twins baseball team will be changed this week to substitute a tax on professional sports logo merchandise for a proposed cigarette tax.

Bob DeBoer, a spokesman for State Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope, the bill's sponsor, said while the lawmaker introduced a bill with a 10-cent increase in the state cigarette tax on Monday, the bill will be amended Thursday to drop that tax hike in favor of other revenue measures.

Those measures would be a wholesale tax on the sale of merchandise carrying professional sports teams' logos, a surcharge on players' salaries and an admissions tax, DeBoer said. He added that estimated revenues from the measures were not available.
Rest will insert the measures in the bill during a Local Government & Metropolitan Affairs Committee hearing on the legislation scheduled for Thursday, he added. Rest is chairman of the committee.
DeBoer said the cigarette tax hike, supported earlier this year by Gov. Arne Carlson, Rest and others, received a negative reaction from lawmakers who felt it was too much of a general tax.

Other amendments Rest is expected to make to the bill include removing language that would place the stadium in Minneapolis, instead saying it would be anywhere in the seven-county metropolitan area. Rest will also propose the formation of a state-wide commission on policy issues related to the stadium, DeBoer said.

A financing plan unveiled last month for the $250 million to $300 million stadium calls for the state to raise about $200 million for the project. In return, the Twins would give the state a 49 percent stake in the team, worth an estimated $51 million.
The Twins would also contribute $15 million to the stadium, as well as apply up to $25 million of upfront revenues, such as naming rights.
